_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Greece covering Minoan Crete (~3000-1450 BCE), Mycenaean civilisation, Greek Dark Ages, city-states (Athens/Sparta), Greco-Persian Wars (Marathon 490 BCE, Thermopylae/Salamis 480 BCE), Athenian Golden Age (Pericles, Parthenon, Socrates/Plato/Aristotle), Peloponnesian War, Alexander the Great, Hellenistic period, Roman conquest 146 BCE, Byzantine Empire (Constantinople, 1000+ years), Ottoman rule (1453-1821), Greek War of Independence (1821-29), modern kingdom, Balkan Wars, WWI/WWII (OXI Day, Italian+German occupation, famine, resistance), Civil War (1946-49), military junta (1967-74), Third Hellenic Republic, EU membership 1981, debt crisis 2010-18.

religion.note: Greek Orthodox Church central to national identity (autocephalous since 1833); Mount Athos (monastic republic, women banned); state-church not fully separated; Islam in Thrace (Ottoman-era minority, Treaty of Lausanne 1923); no civil marriage until 1982; national identity deeply intertwined with Orthodoxy

ethnic_groups.name: Greek
ethnic_groups.notes: Hellenic identity; regional variation (Cretan, Pontic, Aromanian, Sarakatsani); diaspora massive (~7M worldwide, US/Australia/Germany); Megali Idea (Great Idea, irredentism 19th-20th century); philotimo (honour/love of honour) cultural concept

ethnic_groups.name: Albanian
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest immigrant group; mostly post-1991 economic migration; integration improving; Arvanites (Albanian-speaking Greeks, distinct, centuries-old community)

ethnic_groups.name: Bulgarian/Macedonian
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Greece; name dispute with North Macedonia (resolved 2019 Prespa Agreement)

ethnic_groups.name: Romanian/Vlach
ethnic_groups.notes: Aromanian communities (nomadic shepherds historically); declining language

ethnic_groups.name: Turkish
ethnic_groups.notes: Western Thrace Muslim minority (~100k); Treaty of Lausanne protected; mufti appointments contentious; excluded from 1923 population exchange

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Roma (~265k), Pakistani, Georgian, Ukrainian; refugee crisis 2015-16 (Lesbos/Greek islands, gateway to Europe)

independence.from: Ottoman Empire (War of Independence 1821-1829); recognised by Treaty of Constantinople 1832

country_profile.notes_unique: Cradle of Western civilisation (democracy born in Athens ~508 BCE, Cleisthenes); philosophy (Socrates/Plato/Aristotle, foundations of Western thought); Olympic Games (first 776 BCE Olympia, revived Athens 1896); Parthenon (447-432 BCE, Elgin Marbles controversy with UK); Homer (Iliad, Odyssey); tragedy (Sophocles/Euripides) and comedy (Aristophanes); Hippocrates (medicine); Archimedes/Euclid (mathematics); Alexander the Great (conquered Persian Empire, spread Hellenism); 6,000+ islands (227 inhabited); OXI Day (October 28, 1940, rejection of Mussolini's ultimatum); debt crisis (2010-18, worst peacetime economic collapse, 25% GDP lost, troika bailouts €289B, Grexit fears, austerity); 18 UNESCO World Heritage Sites; shipping (largest merchant fleet in world by tonnage); tourism (~30M/year, 20%+ GDP)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Kyriakos Mitsotakis
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: New Democracy (centre-right); second term; son of PM Konstantinos Mitsotakis (political dynasty); Harvard/Stanford educated; moderniser; strong majority; wiretapping scandal (Predator spyware); economic recovery from debt crisis; migration hardliner; re-elected landslide June 2023

head_of_state.name: Katerina Sakellaropoulou
head_of_state.title: President
head_of_state.notes: First female president; former Council of State judge; environmental law specialist; ceremonial role; re-elected 2025

former_leaders.name: Alexis Tsipras
former_leaders.notes: SYRIZA (radical left); youngest PM in 150 years (40); elected on anti-austerity platform; called referendum (OXI vote 61% against bailout July 2015); then accepted bailout anyway (controversial U-turn); Prespa Agreement (North Macedonia name, 2019); resigned after election loss

former_leaders.name: Antonis Samaras
former_leaders.notes: New Democracy; austerity implementation; coalition with PASOK; Golden Dawn crisis; recovery beginning

former_leaders.name: George Papandreou
former_leaders.notes: PASOK; revealed true deficit (12.7% vs reported 6%); triggered debt crisis; IMF bailout; proposed referendum (forced out by EU pressure); son/grandson of PMs (dynasty)

former_leaders.name: Konstantinos Karamanlis (nephew)
former_leaders.notes: New Democracy; 2004 Athens Olympics (successful but expensive, €9B); fires 2007; pre-crisis spending

former_leaders.name: Costas Simitis
former_leaders.notes: PASOK; eurozone entry 2001 (later revealed: cooked books with Goldman Sachs); moderniser; Imia crisis with Turkey

former_leaders.name: Andreas Papandreou
former_leaders.notes: PASOK founder; first socialist PM; charismatic; EU entry 1981; populist; anti-American rhetoric but stayed in NATO; scandals; died in office 1996

nodes.description: The revelation of Greece's true deficit (2009), three international bailout programs totaling €289 billion, savage austerity measures, GDP contraction of 25%, Syriza's rise, the 2015 OXI referendum, and capital controls.

sub_clusters.name: Recovery and Contemporary Challenges
sub_clusters.description: Greece's exit from the final bailout program (August 2018), the return of Mitsotakis and New Democracy, gradual economic recovery, the migration crisis, and the devastating 2023 Thessaly floods.
